newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian minister critical of BHP closure.
newsitem.headline: Australian minister critical of BHP closure.

text.p: Australian finance minister John Fahey said on Thursday that the decision by Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd to close its Newcastle steelworks was given at short notice and could have been handled better by the nation's largest company.
"I thought it was pretty poor public relations on behalf of BHP. I think it could have been handled better," Fahey said in answer to questions at a Property Council of Australia luncheon.
He said he believed government should not interfere in the private sector but "it would have helped if we (the government) had had some notice"

BHP appeared to have ignored the Newcastle community in making its decision. "BHP only represents one percent of the Newcastle workforce but there is nothing more symbolic than the Big Australian saying 'we're closing down,'" Fahey said.
BHP said in late April that it would end steelmaking at Newcastle, its oldest plant which is located north of Sydney in the state of New South Wales, in 1999 at a cost of 2,500 jobs.
BHP will continue to produce steel at its key plant of Port Kembla, south of Sydney, and at Whyalla in South Australia.
When the announcement was made on April 29, the federal government said it was disappointed about the closure but believed it was inevitable given marketplace pressures.
